assertions.finding: At the 70B scale, Orion, Jupiter, and EdgeShard were the successful distributed solutions, with Orion outperforming Jupiter and EdgeShard.
assertions.locator: 4.2. Latency on Llama-2 Models of Varying Scales
assertions.excerpt: all successful distributed solutions, Orion remained the most efficient with an 18,665 ms latency, significantly outperforming Jupiter (27,264 ms) and EdgeShard (43,058 ms).

assertions.finding: Post-training quantization from FP32 to 0.8 bits/element reduces per-hop transmission time by approximately 40 times at an effective rate of 12 Mbit/s.
assertions.excerpt: the transition from FP32 to post-training compression of 0.8 bits/element [15, 16] reduces transmission time by approximately 40 times - from 4.9 s to 122.8 ms per hop at a rate of 12 Mbit/s (Fig. 2).

quantitative.conditions: post-training compression of 0.8 bits/element at R = 12 Mbit/s under L2 encapsulation

assertions.finding: In Stage 2, when one UAV (UAV#3) became unavailable, the eCoEI inference process continued uninterrupted at a lower speed of 2 FPS.
assertions.excerpt: The inference process was not interrupted, but at a lower speed, 2 FPS, in the experiment.

quantitative.workload: collaborative DNN inference over video stream
quantitative.conditions: Stage 2 with one UAV unavailable (UAV#3 communication program disabled)

assertions.finding: In Stage 3, after the unavailable UAV's communication program was recovered, collaborative inference speed reverted to the previous Stage 1 level.
assertions.excerpt: Third, the communication program of the UAV mentioned above was recovered. The collaborative inference speed reverted to the previous level in the first stage.
